summary: Lattice observation tower in Manatee County, mapped with the alternate name Manasota Fire Control Headquarters; sources give only its location, map tags and register absence.

corrections.why: T35S R18E is a land-survey township and range, not an agency. The eastern lookouts listing gives this string as the location with no agency named. Clear the field; a reviewer should decide whether any agency is documented.

evidence.supports: the OpenStreetMap node is named Bradenton Fire Tower
the eastern lookouts listing places the tower in Manatee County
the eastern lookouts listing gives the township as T35S (range 18 East)
the eastern lookouts listing gives the location as township 35 South, range 18 East
Bradenton is the county seat and largest city of Manatee County
evidence.quote: Its county seat and largest city is Bradenton

evidence.supports: Mapcarta gives the alternate name Manasota Fire Control Headquarters
the National Historic Lookout Register lists 31 Florida lookouts; none is Bradenton
evidence.quote: There are 31 lookouts registered in Florida.

evidence.supports: the Former Fire Lookout Sites register lists six former sites in Florida; none is Bradenton
evidence.quote: There are 6 former lookout sites registered in Florida.

notes_for_editor: Thin record. No source read gives a build date, builder, staffing, notable fires, fate, access or current condition, so the story leaves those out. The brief's agency field holds the township label T35S R18E, not an agency; see the proposed correction. The alternate name comes from a Mapcarta page whose origin was not checked, so the story labels it as an alternate name only. The brief's coordinates (27.446625, -82.500552) match the OSM and Mapcarta points. A Natural Atlas search snippet describes the tower as on Gap Creek, but the cached page did not show that text, so it is left out. anyplaceamerica returned HTTP 403 and was not used. The osm.json pipeline flags this node as standing; that is a map flag, not a check. No photos found.
